name: Eton (Vanuatu)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Thieberger, Nicholas. 2004. Topics in the grammar and documentation of South Efate, an Oceanic language of Central Vanuatu. PhD thesis, University of Melbourne (published 2006 as Oceanic Linguistics Special Publication 33).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §3.5.4 Stress (pp. 71-73) is about South Efate/Nafsan, not Eton: 'Stress is not contrastive in South Efate'; initial stress on monomorphemic roots, stress on the first syllable after the article na-, a few penultimate-stressed plant names. Eton appears only in the dialect discussion (p. 42, citing Clark 1985 and Tryon 1976 cognate percentages).

sources.citation: Clark, Ross. 1985. The Efate dialects. Te Reo 28: 3-35.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative phonology of the Efate dialects with first-hand Eton/Epau/Pang-pang data. On stress it says only (pp. 17-19): 'Counting long vowels as two, word stress in Nguna falls on the third last vowel; again, evidence on the other dialects is not so clear', fn. 12 p. 32 citing Schutz 1969b for Nguna. No Eton-specific stress statement; Eton figures in segmental correspondences and final/medial vowel-loss rules (pp. 19-20).

sources.citation: Billington, Rosey. 2019-. Documenting speech and language practices in Eton. ELDP project 0610-SG0594; ELAR deposit SO_93e83e94-e9e3-4f85-bac7-999a6c75ef92.
sources.note: Archive listing only: 40 items (39 audio, 32 video), elicitation/narrative/dictionary material with Eddie Karris, Jeremiah Karris, Linmas Kalsilik; one item 'Checking some words for vowel length'. No written phonology, sketch or stress statement in the listing.

sources.citation: Lynch, John & Terry Crowley. 2001. Languages of Vanuatu: A new survey and bibliography. Pacific Linguistics 517. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 L96 2001)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 L96 2001
sources.note: Survey, pp. 108-111: Eton and Epau 'speak divergent varieties which Clark (pers. comm.) indicates are transitional between South Efate and Nakanamanga'; 'the only published sources for this language are Tryon's (1976) vocabularies from Pango, Eratap and Eton, as well as some additional material.. in Clark (1985a)'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. 1976. New Hebrides languages: An internal classification. Pacific Linguistics C-50. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number PL6211.N44 T7
sources.note: Eton = list 156 (Efate); the phonology chapter is a table of proto-phoneme reflexes per communalect plus wordlists. Nothing on stress for Eton; the only 'stressed/unstressed' mentions are footnotes conditioning *p reflexes in Santo lists (e.g. Sakau). pp. 92-93 treat North and South Efate as separate languages with Eton a dialect of South Efate.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. 1972. The languages of the New Hebrides: A checklist and general survey. Pacific Linguistics A-35 (Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia 3): 43-84.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Checklist only; 'Eton-Epau' listed as dialect 7 of 'Efatese'. Nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Billington, Rosey (with Eddie Karris, Jeremiah Karris, Linmas Kalsilik). 2019-. Documenting speech and language practices in Eton (ELDP 0610-SG0594; ELAR deposit) and any resulting phonological description of Eton.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only modern first-hand documentation of Eton, by a phonetician who has published prominence studies of neighbouring Nafsan; a written phonology or sketch from this project would be the first Eton stress statement. As of this download the deposit holds audio/video only and her ORCID lists no Eton publication.

sources.citation: Thieberger, Nicholas. 2006. A Grammar of South Efate: An Oceanic Language of Vanuatu. Oceanic Linguistics Special Publication 33. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press.

sources.note: Published version of the 2004 thesis held by the project; §3.5.4 gives the stress system of the closest described variety (Eton/Epau are transitional between South Efate and Nakanamanga per Lynch & Crowley 2001). Not Eton itself.

sources.note: Source of the Nguna accent statement (pp. 10-11) that Clark 1985 relies on; describes Nakanamanga/North Efate, the northern pole of the chain Eton belongs to, not Eton.
